newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PTT and Bangchak raise retail oil prices.
newsitem.headline: Thai PTT and Bangchak raise retail oil prices.

text.p: State-run Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) and Banchak Petroleum Plc said on Wednesday they had raised retail oil prices to reflect higher costs after the baht's de facto devaluation.
Bangchak increased pump prices by 15 satangs (five US cents) per litre across the board while PTT, the country's leader in retail oil business, hiked prices by 12-15 satang.
Other major oil companies such as Caltex, Esso and Shell raised their pump prices by 18 percent since last week.
Diesel and petrol prices currently stand around 8.45 and 9.58 respectively after the adjustment.

The baht has depreciated to around 29.00-3.00 baht per dollar from around 25.10 since it was released from a peg to a basket of currencies dominated by the dollar into a managed float system on July 2.
Oil industry sources estimated that if the baht stayed around 28.00-29.00 to the dollar, retail oil prices would rise by 25-50 satang per litre.
